- **Region**: inclusive bounds selected the 0.02°-grid cells at 57.58–58.76 °N, 10.26–11.44 °E; 3304 sea cells (finite on all 92 target days), 296 land cells.
- **Climatology/threshold**: day-of-year mapping 1–366 (29 Feb = 60, non-leap years skip it); pools = ±5 calendar days around each 1992–2002 baseline date, including the window extensions (all 4028 days of 1991-12-27→2003-01-05 used; every pool holds 121 values per cell; day 60 gets no pool). Threshold = 90th percentile with MATLAB-default quantile (numpy `method="hazen"`); climatology = pool mean; day 60 set to the mean of days 59/61 (raw values were numerically identical, so this is a no-op here); both smoothed with the wrap-around centred 31-day moving mean (verified exactly against an independent loop implementation).
- **Per-cell MHWs**: 18 382 hot cell-days over 2004-06-01→2004-08-31; 2 356 per-cell MHWs — exactly one per sea cell (lengths 5–10 days) — all part of one coherent regional warming episode. Run/gap-join logic (qualify ≥5 first, then join 1–2-day gaps only) was validated on synthetic test cases.
- **Regional events**: **1 event, onset 2004-08-05, end 2004-08-15** (11 consecutive active days).

**Outputs written**:
- `output/mhw_mask.nc` — `mhw` uint8, dims (time=92, lat=60, lon=60), dataset coordinate values, land cells 0; read-back matches the computed mask exactly.
- `output/report.json` — region, baseline_analysed (1991-12-27→2003-01-05, the extended pool window actually used), target_analysed (2004-06-01→2004-08-31), the single event, `complete: true`, and a caveat noting the 0.02° cell-centre selection and pool construction.
